title: Why $50/day online keeps Jack Friks happily unemployed: autonomy and scalable leverage
summary: Jack reflects on hitting about $50/day from an app with premium features, and why that small number buys autonomy and keeps him out of a job. He argues for owning a scalable product, helping people genuinely, and treating paying users as real validation.

principles.text: Aim for autonomy, not just income: a small online income can keep a job away and fund time freedom.
principles.quote: if you want you can escape that cycle of the job okay you don't have to I'm not saying everyone should I'm just saying if you you could

principles.text: Prefer owning scalable leverage: a built product makes $50 and $500 a day with about the same effort.
principles.quote: for me to make $50 a day versus me to make 500 it's about the same amount of effort

principles.text: A built product doesn't have to be rebuilt per sale, so marginal cost is tiny and revenue can scale.
principles.quote: I've already made the app people are paying for the to use the apps uh premium features or take away ads whatever may be and I don't have to make that again every time when someone buys the thing so it's scalable

principles.text: Profit only comes from genuinely helping people; aim to over-deliver on value.
principles.quote: that's the only way to do anything really um that makes profits or makes a money is to actually help people otherwise you're running a fugazi

principles.text: Paying customers are far stronger validation than kind comments and keep you going.
principles.quote: people paying me for my product that maybe this actually could work and actually it can because people are paying me for it and they're telling me they like it which is IM immensely more valuable than people just commenting

principles.text: Owning the business means you capture the full upside and see direct cause and effect.
principles.quote: any awards you make are going to come back right to you which is really good if I make $10,000 because it had a really good day or something well guess what I don't just get paid a bonus I get paid the $10,000
